BiblicalUsage: This word is used once, for the thought of a man at ease about a man who slips. Job says he that is ready to slip with his feet is as a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease, and the friends who sit in comfort despise the lamp that is going out.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for the thought of the comfortable carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the warning, that the man at ease despises the lamp that is about to go out, and calls it wisdom.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
